Ocular Therapeutix beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $13.48 million, flat year on year. It was an exceptional quarter for the company, with a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is Ocular Therapeutix a buy or sell going into earnings?

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Ocular Therapeutix’s revenue to decline 4.3% year on year, improving from the 5.7% decrease it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Ocular Therapeutix has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at Ocular Therapeutix’s peers in the pharmaceuticals segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Elanco delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 11.3%, beating analysts’ expectations by 4.8%, and Jazz Pharmaceuticals reported revenues up 10.4%, topping estimates by 2.8%. Jazz Pharmaceuticals traded up 7.1% following the results.

There has been positive sentiment among investors in the pharmaceuticals segment, with share prices up 4.8% on average over the last month. Ocular Therapeutix is down 10.8% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $25.45 (compared to the current share price of $6.72).
